assets.name: rook-harbor
assets.prompt:
Use case: illustration-story
Asset type: Original Rookstride website hero and mascot reference, landscape 1536x1024.
Primary request: Create an editorial comic illustration of Rook, an original helpful red bird navigator, on a rooftop looking across a small fantastical harbor city at dusk. He holds a folded cream map with a simple red route and a tiny brass lantern; a red thread-like path winds toward a distant stone gateway. A warm, capable, optimistic adventure, not a superhero battle.
Subject identity: Rook has a very simple round scarlet-red bird head, two swept feather points on top, a red pointed beak facing right, a single bold white eye patch with a black round pupil, compact pear-shaped scarlet body and small dark feet. His silhouette is unmistakable at small sizes. A dark charcoal short scarf trails behind him, cream canvas satchel. No human face, no hands or arms: expressive wings hold the map. Keep the character graphic and iconic, like a clean original mascot, not a realistic bird.
Style: premium hand-inked European adventure comic, confident thick charcoal contours, flat screenprinted shapes, subtle grain and paper texture; architectural detail restrained. Warm cream #F4F0E7, near-black #141418, signature red #EE3038, muted blue-gray and ochre accents. No gradients or 3D plastic.
Composition: Rook prominent in the right-center foreground, about one third of image height, rooftop at bottom, wide breathing space around his head, arched gateway visible in background, a sweeping route across the city. Elegant cinematic illustration that also works when cropped to a tall rectangle.
Constraints: No lettering, speech bubbles, logos, watermarks, UI, flags or real-world national landmarks. Fully original character and world. The depicted route is fictional lore, not a technical diagram.

assets.name: chapter-1
assets.prompt:
Use case: illustration-story
Asset type: Wordless two-page comic spread, 1536x1152 landscape, for an animated story journal.
Input image 1 is a reference for the exact original bird character Rook and visual world/style. Create a NEW comic composition, preserving his red body, two crest feathers, red right-facing beak, white eye patch, black pupil, charcoal scarf, cream satchel and lantern.
Primary request: Chapter 1, “The borrowed light.” Six rectangular comic panels in an exact 2-column by 3-row grid, equal panel dimensions. Each column is one page; read LEFT column top to bottom, then RIGHT column top to bottom. Narrow warm cream gutters between all panels and a slightly larger gutter in the exact vertical center. NO text or speech bubbles.
Left column panel 1: On the cobbled harbor at night, Rook notices a small cream-colored rabbit courier standing beside an unlit lighthouse, holding a bundle of letters. The rabbit wears a blue coat. Establish a welcoming magical harbor city.
Left column panel 2: Close-up: the rabbit shows Rook a dark lantern; Rook tilts his head with a kind, attentive expression.
Left column panel 3: Rook opens his satchel; a single lit brass lantern casts a warm circle of light on his simple folded map. The rabbit looks hopeful.
Right column panel 1: Rook and the rabbit climb a gently winding stone path together; Rook carries his lamp, pointing with his wing toward the lighthouse. Red scarf trailing.
Right column panel 2: At the lighthouse door, Rook gives the lantern to the rabbit. Focus on the lantern and their faces; an act of help, no human hands, only wings and paws.
Right column panel 3: Wide resolution: the lighthouse shines over the harbor; rabbit delivers letters below and Rook waves from the stone arch. Warm dawn. End upbeat and peaceful.
Style: Same confident charcoal-ink adventure comic as reference, flat screenprinted limited palette, subtle paper grain, warm cream, signal red, muted blue-gray and ochre. Keep Rook's shape consistent in ALL panels. Charming and editorial, not childish stock art.
Constraints: All SIX distinct panels must be present in the strict 2 columns × 3 rows layout. Do not merge panels or insert panels. No lettering, numbers, logos, watermarks, UI, real-world national symbols. Do not imitate an existing franchise.

assets.name: chapter-2
assets.prompt:
Use case: illustration-story
Asset type: Wordless two-page comic spread, 1536x1152 landscape, animated Rookstride field journal.
Input image 1 is the reference for Rook's exact identity and ink/paper adventure-comic style. Preserve the compact scarlet bird, two crest feathers, red pointed beak, white eye patch, black pupil, charcoal scarf, cream satchel and little dark feet. A NEW story in the same original world.
Primary request: Chapter 2, “The noisy market.” Six equal rectangular comic panels in an EXACT 2-column × 3-row grid. Read LEFT column top-to-bottom, then RIGHT column top-to-bottom. Warm cream gutters, slightly wider exact center gutter. NO text, lettering or speech bubbles.
Left column panel 1: Daytime at a harbor market. Rook discovers a kind hedgehog mapmaker at a stall almost hidden by many colorful blank hanging signboards and fluttering ribbons. A small mouse customer cannot find the counter.
Left column panel 2: Close view: the hedgehog looks tired amid tangled strings of signs, trying to show a beautiful paper map to the mouse. Rook listens, one wing to chin.
Left column panel 3: Rook gently unties a jumble of blank banners with his wing while the hedgehog holds a small ladder. Cooperative work, cheerful concentration.
Right column panel 1: Rook is about to remove one small blue signboard showing ONLY a simple hand-painted compass pictogram, no words; the hedgehog kindly points to it, explaining that this particular sign is useful.
Right column panel 2: Rook and the hedgehog place that single blue compass sign neatly above the now-tidy stall. Mouse customer can see the maps.
Right column panel 3: Wide resolution: the open, calm map stall with just the blue compass sign, hedgehog happily giving a folded map to the mouse, Rook sitting on the stall roof smiling. Sunny harbor behind them. Peaceful, upbeat.
Style: Confident thick charcoal ink, flat screenprinted cream/red/blue-gray/ochre palette, subtle paper grain. Same Rook identity as reference across ALL panels. Restrained architectural details. Original charming editorial comic.
Constraints: All six distinct panels in strict grid. Blank signs except the single compass pictogram. No numbers, watermarks, logos, brand names, speech balloons or readable text. No existing cartoon-franchise characters.

assets.name: chapter-3
assets.prompt:
Use case: illustration-story
Asset type: Wordless two-page comic spread, 1536x1152 landscape for Rookstride field journal.
Reference image 1 defines Rook's exact red-bird identity and original adventure-comic world. Preserve red round head and pear-shaped red body, two crest feathers, red pointed beak, white eye patch, black pupil, charcoal scarf, cream satchel, dark small bird feet. NEW story in same charcoal-ink and warm-paper style.
Primary request: Chapter 3, “The bridge that waited.” Six equal rectangular panels in strict 2-column by 3-row grid, with warm cream gutters and slightly wider exact center gutter. Read LEFT column top-to-bottom, then RIGHT column top-to-bottom. NO text, numbers or speech balloons.
Left column panel 1: After a rainstorm, Rook and Tess, a friendly brown otter traveler with a green backpack, arrive at a small damaged wooden footbridge over a narrow creek outside the harbor. A clear gap of missing planks stops them. Both remain on solid ground.
Left column panel 2: Close view: Rook checks a loose splintered plank at the near edge with a wing while Tess waits safely behind him. Thoughtful inspection, no dangerous leap.
Left column panel 3: Rook and Tess turn back onto the stone path, looking at his folded map to find a safe detour. Rook gestures toward the creek's bank, no readable map writing.
Right column panel 1: Rook, Tess, a rabbit neighbor and a hedgehog neighbor cooperate, carrying short boards and a spool of red ribbon along a safe dry bank. Same compact Rook and no human hands.
Right column panel 2: The four neighbors lay a short tidy boardwalk on the muddy bank far from the broken bridge and tie red ribbons at the turns. Everyone safe, purposeful.
Right column panel 3: Warm sun returns: Tess waves as she walks away on the completed short detour; Rook and the two neighbors rest beside the creek and their red-ribbon-marked path. Broken bridge still in distant background; happy resolution.
Style: Confident charcoal ink, flat screenprinted colors, fine grain, cream paper, bright red, muted blue-gray and ochre, lush but restrained environment. Premium original illustrated journal; same character design across panels and previous stories.
Constraints: Exactly six panels, strict 2 columns × 3 rows. No lettering, logos, watermarks, national symbols or franchise characters. Focus on cooperation and choosing a safer route, not action-hero powers.
